abstract: One of the primary challenges in efficiency literature arises from dealing with cases involving datasets with multiple outputs for decision-making units. While Data Envelopment Analysis naturally handles multiple outputs in efficiency calculation, Stochastic Frontier Analysis also effectively accommodates multiple outputs under certain modelling conditions. To estimate a spatial Stochastic Frontier model, we utilized a distinct dataset with multiple outputs, which were consolidated into a single output using a newly developed approach. We applied the methodology to Turkish hospitals and found statistically significant spatial dependence in hospitals’ technical efficiency. The median of efficiency estimates is 79.3%. The mean total output elasticities are 0.1943 for beds, 0.1186 for physicians, 0.3221 for specialist physicians, and 0.3417 for nurses. For the hospitals under consideration, the returns to scale is very close to 1. Our results show the influence of regional factors on hospital performance. These findings highlight the importance of considering spatial interactions and regional policies to improve hospital efficiency.
title: Hospital efficiency in Türkiye via spatial Stochastic Frontier Analysis
title_zh: 土耳其医院效率：基于空间随机前沿分析

abstract: In 2021 we issued a call for papers for a special issue on “Contests: Theory, Evidence and Applications.” We received an enthusiastic response from scholars across a range of fields. The ten articles selected for this volume survived a rigorous peer review process and span a wide range of topics in the growing literature on contests.
abstract_zh: 2021年，我们为“竞赛：理论、证据与应用”特刊发出了论文征稿通知。来自多个领域的学者反响热烈。本卷精选的十篇文章经过严格的同行评审流程，涵盖了竞赛这一日益发展的文献中广泛的主题。
title: Introduction to the special issue on contests: theory, evidence, and applications
